explanation: Defoe placed the island off the mouth of the Orinoco, within sight of Trinidad. The real castaway Alexander Selkirk was marooned in the Pacific, on an island renamed Robinson Crusoe Island in 1966.

claims.text: In Defoe's novel, Robinson Crusoe's island lies off the mouth of the Orinoco River, near Trinidad, in the Atlantic, not in the Pacific.
Defoe places Crusoe's island off the mouth of the Orinoco, within sight of Trinidad.
The Scottish sailor Alexander Selkirk was marooned on Más a Tierra, in the Juan Fernández Islands of the Pacific.
Chile renamed Más a Tierra as Robinson Crusoe Island in 1966.
